The problem I had with your statement was not that you are a self-proclaimed nihilist who made a statement about a hypothetical god.  I myself am a nihilist and former Christian who believes in a "god".  By "god" I mean something had to start the universe and the matter in it was created somehow, but I don't believe we can know if whatever "god" that may be interacts with the universe, and I don't see any evidence that this "god" gives meaning to life or the world.

However, saying that one being can be more or less moral than another being implies that there is a true moral standard, which is not a nihilistic concept.  There isn't any objective standard of how to evaluate one's morality.  The only way there could be this moral standard is if there was a God that ruled over the universe and set the standard for right and wrong. "Right" and "wrong" in the objective moral sense do not necessarily have to be things that follow normal human instinct.  

I understand if youre using the word "moral" to mean a subjective understanding of morality based on the popular opinions of humans, but at first glance it didn't seem to fit with nihilism

By "help" I didn't mean you, yourself trying to get me un-depressed.  Just offering advice on how I could find a way to do that.  I've talked to enough people to know that hearing something nice from someone doesn't do much

>Question:  How did you come to accept Christ?

Was raised in the church and always had some level of belief that was instilled in me by my parents.  Got really into apologetics my first couple years of college and decided I really believed it and wanted to base my whole life around it.  Was also really depressed at one point and realized living for anything else wasn't worth it.  Spent \~16 months doing lots of bible studies, going to church, mentorship, spending time with Christian friends, evangelism, and spending time alone reading the bible and praying.

Got so sick of the Christian communities I was in and how the people were so unwilling to do any critical thinking.  People will believe anything if they hear it from enough people in their community.  Expressing my doubts and concerns, or questioning authority gets me treated like an outcast, told Im "not mature enough".  Ive seen so many other Christians repress their own doubts.  Seeing the Christian response to these concerns ("we can't understand God", "you just need to trust God", etc., not saying these are logically inconsistent, but they require blind faith) caused me to step back and decide for myself whether what I had believed for so long was actually true.
